title: CSPI-MT: Calibrated Safe Policy Improvement with Multiple Testing for Threshold Policies

problem.claim: Safe policy improvement adopts a new policy only when it is better than a specified baseline with at least a pre-specified probability.

gap.claim: Existing safety checks may be underpowered and limit opportunities to find safe improvements, causing frequent reversion to the baseline.

contributions.claim: The approach leverages the most powerful safety test in the asymptotic regime and allows multiple candidate policies to be tested against the baseline.
CSPI and CSPI-MT are algorithms for selecting cutoff values to maximize policy improvement from the baseline for threshold policies.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CSPI and CSPI-MT as novel algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In adversarial settings, the approach controls the rate of adopting a policy worse than the baseline at the pre-specified error level, including at moderate sample sizes.

Synthetic and external dataset experiments report improved detection rates of safe policies and realized improvement, especially under stringent safety requirements and low signal-to-noise conditions.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-risk policy modification requires high-confidence improvement over an existing baseline.
Safe policy improvement adopts a new policy only when it exceeds the baseline with a pre-specified probability.
The work studies threshold policies and addresses underpowered safety checks that restrict safe improvements.
The approach uses a powerful safety test and multiple candidate testing, producing CSPI and CSPI-MT cutoff-selection algorithms.
The authors report error-rate control in adversarial settings and improved detection and realized improvement on synthetic and external datasets.

source_observation.claim: Testing multiple candidate threshold policies is presented as a way to increase opportunities for safe improvement over a baseline.

interpretation.claim: A safety-improvement procedure can trade broader candidate search against controlled adoption risk.

application.claim: In high-risk threshold-based decisions, consider multiple candidate policies while maintaining a pre-specified safety error level.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the approach may fail outside the stated adversarial, moderate-sample, stringent-safety, or low-signal conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the statistical assumptions, test construction, or cutoff-selection procedure.
The abstract does not report dataset identities, sample sizes, baselines, or quantitative results.
